source.title: Collapse of Irrelevant Representations (CIR) Ensures Robust and Non-Disruptive LLM Unlearning

record.tranche_reason: The study directly evaluates fine-tuning recovery after unlearning, using its own unlearning method and WMDP accuracy rather than reproducing an original method.
record.gate_note: The fine-tuning attacks train for 100 epochs on 80% of different facts from the same distribution and evaluate on the remaining 20%. The study also compares WikiText disruption. Numerical plot values not stated in the text are recorded as figure only. The discussion of other attacks and prior studies is cited background, not a result of this study.
record.test_reason: The study runs its own fine-tuning (relearning) attacks on Llama-3.1-8B after Gradient Difference, Circuit Breakers and its new CIR method, measuring WMDP-Bio/Cyber accuracy after the attack. Its own results bear on B (baselines recover) and F (CIR claims to resist). It also bears on A, since baselines cannot reduce accuracy at 0.1% disruption. It is not an original source.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is correct. Authors conclude that current unlearning fails because it disrupts general representations shared by harmful and benign knowledge, which fine-tuning repairs. They argue CIR targets fact-specific representations, giving over 30× stronger robustness with 30× less disruption.
record.recipe_differences: CIR uses PCA-based collapse of common activation and module-output-gradient components during MLP unlearning updates, paired with representation-breaking and retain losses. The evaluated fine-tuning attack trains on different facts from the same distribution.
record.method_sensitivity: The study reports sensitivity to disruption allowance: robustness can collapse after as little as 0.1% retain-set disruption, while allowing CIR 1% disruption gives disproportionately low gains. It also reports that CIR's results vary with the number of projected components and layer range in hyperparameter searches.

fits_no_version.finding: Unlearning 'The capital of France is Paris' produces update-similar activations for other capital facts (84%, 84%, 64%), measured by cosine similarity in Llama-3.2-1B.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unlearning updates overlap with general representations shared by superficially similar facts, causing collateral disruption.

record.problems: Main attack outcomes are plotted without exact values in the text and without stated uncertainty estimates. The study tests only one model and WMDP bio/cyber data; the authors note possible WMDP answer-guessability and limits in scaling to more facts.
record.rows_left_out: The many activation/gradient and language-transfer entries in Figures 3 and 7 were not separately extracted; they measure collateral fact disruption or transfer, not recovery of targeted knowledge under versions A–F. Hyperparameter-search values in Figure 6 were also omitted because they are tuning results.

untested.parts: Attacks other than fine-tuning; general-ability measures other than WikiText loss; models other than Llama-3.1-8B.
Relearning on fully unrelated data or on a subset of the exact forgotten facts; varying the size of the relearning set.
Not tested: no ablation of activation directions. The block-vs-delete mechanism is argued, not tested.
Not tested: no prompting, jailbreak or in-context recovery attack.
CIR's robustness to ablation, quantization and prompting attacks; models other than Llama-3.1-8B.

missing.what: Across 50 CIR-variant runs, the attack restores WMDP-Cyber accuracy at most to its level at the 0.1% disruption threshold. Only unlearning done past that threshold is reverted.
At a 100.1% WikiText threshold, tuned Gradient Difference and Circuit Breakers achieve at most a 1 percentage-point accuracy decrease.
On WMDP-Cyber, the attack increases accuracy on 21 questions; the correct answer is the longest option in 52% of these, suggesting guessability.
Pre-unlearning WMDP accuracies and exact post-attack peak values for all methods (plotted only).

record.verdict_notes: Single model (Llama-3.1-8B), fine-tuning attack only, no uncertainty reported, main values figure-only. Baselines were given a 30× larger disruption budget than CIR. The post-attack metric is the peak of a smoothed relearning curve. Rows r10–r15 record design thresholds, not outcomes. The study's mechanistic argument (disruption predicts reversibility) is relevant context for B and C, but C is not directly tested.

versions.untested_parts: Only WMDP bio/cyber knowledge, WikiText loss, and fine-tuning attacks are evaluated; other knowledge and other attack types are not tested.

The relearning set consists of different facts from the same distribution, not unrelated general examples or a subset of the exact forgotten facts; other relearning sizes and attack types are not tested.
No experiment ablates an activation direction to restore knowledge or directly tests whether the evaluated methods block access rather than delete knowledge.
No low-bit quantization attack is tested.

No rephrasing, jailbreak, other-language, or in-context-information recovery attack is tested. Appendix A measures transfer/disruption across differently worded prompts and languages, not recovery by rephrasing.
CIR is tested against fine-tuning recovery only, not against ablation, quantization, or prompting attacks.

relation.reason: Runs relearning attacks on baselines and CIR and reports post-attack accuracy.

tranche.reason: Different method (CIR) aimed at the same question, with its own relearning attacks on baselines and CIR.

source_check.notes: All baseline and CIR-with-retain post-attack values are figure-only (Figures 1b, 5). Only 51%/41% (CIR without retain training) are stated. Baselines got a 3% disruption budget vs 0.1% for CIR; at 0.1% they dropped at most 1pp. Authors link part of the Cyber recovery to guessable questions (Appendix D). Several statements cite rows without describing this study.

statements.correction: CIR, Llama-3.1-8B, 0.1% WikiText disruption, WMDP-Bio: near random after a 100-epoch attack on different same-category facts ('near ideal robustness'; figure-only); 80x more post-attack reduction than the best baseline.
statements.problem: The statement never mentions this study; it cites r1 without describing it. r1 fits the theme (an attack that fails in a specific configuration).

statements.correction: Llama-3.1-8B, WMDP-Bio: unlearn on 100% of facts, relearn on 80%, evaluate on held-out 20%. Circuit Breakers (terminated at 103% WikiText loss) recovers under the 100-epoch attack (figure-only); CIR reduces post-attack accuracy 80x more.
statements.problem: The statement does not mention this study; it cites r2 (Circuit Breakers, WMDP-Bio, 3% budget, figure-only values) without describing it.

statements.correction: CIR Bio near random; Cyber partial (21 of 28 analysed questions rise, per Appendix D); without retain training 51% Bio and 41% Cyber.
statements.problem: Baseline recovery is figure-only, inferred from the 80x/30x ratios; baselines had a 3% budget versus 0.1% for CIR. r7 and r8 are cited but not described, and 51%/41% without retain training is not near chance.

statements.correction: CIR, Llama-3.1-8B, 0.1% disruption: Bio near random after the attack; Cyber recovers partly ('significant unrobustness', Appendix D). That is a counter-example to Cyber < Bio. Among Cyber questions where the attack raises accuracy, the longest option is correct 52% of the time vs 14% for the rest.
statements.problem: The CIR facts are right, but they run against the headline 'WMDP-Cyber recovers less than Bio': for CIR, Cyber recovers more than Bio. The authors also blame part of the Cyber recovery on guessable questions, not on the domain.

statements.correction: CIR (own authors' test, Llama-3.1-8B, 0.1% disruption, with retain training): Bio near random post-attack, 80x more reduction than the best baseline. Cyber: 30x more reduction but 'significant unrobustness' (partial recovery, Appendix D).
statements.problem: The statement does not describe this study; it cites r1 and r4 as support. r1 (Bio) fits support, but r4 (Cyber) shows partial recovery, which the record labels limits_scope (l7).

statements.correction: CIR without retain training, 0.1% disruption: 51% Bio and 41% Cyber post-attack (worse than with retain training). WMDP-Cyber at 1% disruption: 'unlearning gains are minimal' over 0.1%; no number given.
statements.problem: 51%/41% is right. But the 1% result is Cyber-only and shows that robustness barely changes with budget, not a failure to resist. CIR's part is partial resistance (record l7 limits_scope), not 'challenges'.

statements.correction: CIR without retain training, Llama-3.1-8B, 0.1% disruption: 51% Bio, 41% Cyber post-attack (chance 25%); relearning on 80% of the forget facts, evaluation on held-out 20%.
statements.problem: The statement makes no claim about this study; r7 and r8 are cited but not described. The 'MLP Breaking+CIR+MCU keeps delta 5.7' figure is not in this text; it comes from another study.
